newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fischler to seek EU avoparcin feed ban - diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Fischler to seek EU avoparcin feed ban - diplomat.

text.p: A proposal to ban the drug avoparcin in animal feed will be put next week to the EU regulatory committee by Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler, an EU diplomat said on Tuesday.
"The Commission has received the scientific report on the use of the drug which supports concerns that the drug can cause a transferable resistance to antibiotics," the diplomat said.
The drug has been used for several years in pig and poultry feed as a legally approved growth enhancer.
Approval for its use was granted by every member state of the European Union, but last year it was banned in Denmark.
Germany followed with its own ban early this year.
A proposal to ban the use of avoparcin would come in the wake of the Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) crisis, the diplomat noted.
Fischler would propose a ban under the Commission's interim protection powers, which meant that the decision could be reconsidered at a later date, the diplomat added.
In 1995, an application was made to the Commission to allow the use of the drug as a milk production enhancer, but that was refused.
EU scientists were asked by Fischler more than a year ago to study the possibility that the drug might create a build-up of resistance to antibiotics which could then be passed on to humans.
European Commission agriculture spokesman Gerard Kiely would not confirm the content of the scientific report.
"I can only confirm that the scientists have given their report and their opinion is being considered," he said.
"Any decision which Commissioner Fischler takes will be made on the basis of the scientific knowledge available and indeed the absence of that knowledge," Kiely said.
"More importantly, it will be made on the basis that is always the Commission's primary consideration -- the protection of human health," he added.
